clue.text: Sound of the dying provides amusement for the newborn

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the throaty noise of laboured breathing at the end of life
second meaning: a baby's toy that clatters when shaken

explanation.surface: A grim image of a deathbed noise somehow entertaining a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links life's end and its start; the answer is both the death rattle and the baby's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A death rattle is the noise of laboured breathing near death, and a baby's rattle is a shaken toy.

clue.text: Two soldiers rolling dice with Cromwell, for instance

indicators.note: rolling dice tumbles them, so these letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers gambling at dice alongside Oliver Cromwell in the Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell signed the death warrant of King Charles I in 1649.
explanation.definitionFit: A regicide is someone who kills a monarch; Cromwell was among those who condemned Charles I.

clue.text: Speculate: put extra money under the Ring

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means being placed below it, so this piece follows

parts.note: a pay rise is extra money

explanation.surface: Betting extra money on a Wagner production of the Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Ring look like Wagner's opera cycle, but it is just a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form ideas or conjectures without proof, much as speculating does.

clue.text: Film director may mislay young principal

indicators.note: a principal is the chief or first, so only the opening letter counts

explanation.surface: A movie director in danger of misplacing a youthful head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Losey directed The Servant and The Go-Between.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Losey was an American-born filmmaker who worked mainly in Britain after being blacklisted.

clue.text: Industrial waste produced mainly by the well off

definitions.text: Industrial waste produced mainly by the well off

parts.words: produced mainly by the well off
parts.note: setter's reading: the word for this waste is, letter for letter, nearly the word for wealthy, differing only in its first vowel

explanation.surface: A social complaint that the rich cause most of the pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: EFFLUENT is mainly AFFLUENT (well off): only the first letter differs, so 'mainly' is a hint at the near-identical spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent is liquid discharge from factories or sewage works, the standard term for industrial outflow.

clue.text: Tense Utopian?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'will have done'
second meaning: a flawless time to come, as an ideal world would be

explanation.surface: A nervous dreamer of ideal societies.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective meaning anxious, but it is the grammar noun; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The future perfect is a verb tense, and a Utopian dreams of a perfect time to come.

clue.text: Shun clone cooked for meals

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or altered, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Avoiding a cloned animal served up as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Luncheons are formal midday meals, the term being an older word for lunch.

clue.text: Chaperone (French) is outside — blimey!

indicators.note: being outside something surrounds it, so the French word wraps the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A shocked French chaperone standing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor and blimey are both British exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies someone for protection or propriety, exactly as a chaperone does.

clue.text: Also came first in Spanish city

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: to come first in a race is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone also won a race in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, once its capital and famous for swords.

clue.text: Surmise that theatre cat will accept quarters

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it inside, so the cat's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Gus is the Theatre Cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum poems and the musical Cats
two of the four compass quarters, east and south

explanation.surface: Speculating that a stage cat will take lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are the compass points; E and S sit inside GUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmise is to suppose without proof, which is what a guess does; both are verbs.

clue.text: Concerning plants restored to Caliban

indicators.note: something restored has been put back together, here into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Caliban, the island savage of The Tempest, is given back his plant lore.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical is the adjective for things relating to botany, the scientific study of vegetation.

clue.text: Talent show?

parts.note: surface reading: a variety competition for singers and acts
setter's reading: talent is British slang for attractive people, so a show of talent is a contest of good looks

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'the talent' means good-looking people, which turns a show of skills into a parade of looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty pageant puts attractive contestants on display to be judged, a show of slang talent.

clue.text: Head waves to young travellers resting in dog den

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: something resting in a place lies inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: an animal's den is its lair
YH is youth hostel, where young travellers stay

explanation.surface: Young backpackers bed down in a dog's den, a sort of travel mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: Youth hostels are where young travellers rest, abbreviated in Britain as YH.
explanation.definitionFit: Waves on one's head are curls, so curly hair describes a head of wavy locks.

clue.text: Goody would be Biblical baddy

parts.note: the goody in a story is its hero
'd is the contracted form of would

explanation.surface: A paradox: the good guy turning out to be a villain of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Goody would' as HERO'D. Herod the Great ordered the Massacre of the Innocents.
explanation.definitionFit: King Herod is the villain of the Nativity story who ordered infants slaughtered in Bethlehem.

clue.text: Conversely, no work emphasised means of finishing meal

indicators.note: conversely means the other way round, so the whole string is read from its end

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A slogan about doing no work, oddly linked to the end of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: OP, short for opus, is a standard crossword abbreviation for a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert spoon is the utensil used to eat the pudding course that ends a meal.

clue.text: Outrageous example: 51 lost from among the faithful

indicators.note: something lost from among a group has gone missing out of it, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: A shocking case of fifty-one people leaving a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The faithful' reads as a noun phrase, and the religious as a noun means the devout.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means shockingly bad or flagrant, as an outrageous act is.

clue.text: Anticipate being curtailed with regard to woodland

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to forestall is to anticipate and prevent

explanation.surface: Expecting to be cut short in a discussion about trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestal is the adjective for things relating to forests, so it concerns wooded land.

clue.text: Skinny chap could be an east European

parts.note: a Pole comes from Poland in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Guessing a thin man's nationality from his build.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the words literally: BE AN POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is an informal term for a very tall, thin person, like the stick for climbing beans.

clue.text: Grey 7, or assortment from the corner shop

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Picking a grey Ford Escort or some other mix at a local store.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Escort was a popular British car, which the cross-reference brings to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner shop is a small local grocer selling everyday food and household goods.

clue.text: Tom has risen? What sauce!

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone's cheek after Tom gets out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What sauce!' sounds like an outburst at impudence, but it simply defines a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is a variant spelling of ketchup, the tomato condiment, so it is a sauce.

clue.text: Active type brings servicemen in the window

indicators.note: to bring someone in is to take them inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: an active person is a doer

explanation.surface: An energetic person letting soldiers in through the window.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is an upright window projecting from a sloping roof, often in an attic.

clue.text: Included a cat going round the pole

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the cat's letters wrap about the pole

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
N is north, one of the poles

explanation.surface: A cat circling a maypole, joining in the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Mog, short for moggy, is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be among a group is to be counted within it, so the preposition matches being included.

clue.text: Check back on street for oriental in German viticultural town

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: to check a horse is to rein it in
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone stops on a street in a German wine town to make way for an easterner.
explanation.walkthrough: NIER from REIN backwards, then ST, E and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nierstein is a Rhineland town famous for vineyards and the white wine named after it.

clue.text: Bit of froth or sweat

parts.note: a single sud is one bubble of suds

explanation.surface: Is that bubbly stuff foam or perspiration?
explanation.walkthrough: Sudor is the Latin word for sweat, used in medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudor is a technical medical term for perspiration, borrowed directly from Latin.

clue.text: Wanting to sleep during the approach to Southampton? A thousand times no!

indicators.note: during places one thing in the midst of another, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the Solent is the strait leading into Southampton Water
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
'times' sets two pieces side by side like a product, joining NO to the previous piece

explanation.surface: A drowsy sailor heading into Southampton refusing a thousand times over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland Hampshire that ships use to reach Southampton.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent describes drowsiness, the feeling of craving rest; both are adjectival phrases.

clue.text: During party, a non-drinker has the same again

indicators.note: during puts one thing inside the span of another, so the party encloses the rest

parts.note: a means one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A teetotaller at a party orders the same again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests another round of drinks, ironic for a non-drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is the word used to repeat what was just said, meaning likewise or another of those.

clue.text: Leech and Peel having a sit-in

indicators.note: having means holding within, so the first word wraps around the rest
in places the following words inside, completing the instruction to hold them

parts.note: to pare fruit is to peel it

explanation.surface: Two figures, Leech and Peel, staging a protest sit-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Leech and Peel look like surnames; Leech is the definition and Peel the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, and figuratively a person who lives off others, a sponger.

clue.text: Partition makes headless giant internally sick

indicators.note: internally means inside, so the next word goes within the shortened one
without a head means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: an ogre is a monstrous giant

explanation.surface: A beheaded giant feeling sick inside, a grisly fairy-tale image.
explanation.walkthrough: OGRE loses O to give GRE, which holds ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating of bars used as a screen or divider, such as in a confessional.
